semantic_correction.stem: A nurse is preparing an oral medication. According to the Open RN medication-administration checklist, when should the medication label be compared with the MAR as part of the three label checks?

options.A: Compare the label with the MAR when the medication is removed from storage, again while it is being prepared, and again at the bedside before administration.
options.B: Compare the label with the MAR during preparation and after administration, then complete the third comparison when the medication record is documented.
options.C: Compare the label with the MAR at the bedside before administration and twice afterward, using documentation to confirm that the correct medication was given.
options.D: Compare the label with the MAR during preparation and at the bedside, and omit the remaining comparison when barcode scanning confirms the medication.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/Open RN Nursing Skills guidance states that the medication label must be checked for name, dose, and route and compared with the medication administration record at least three different times: when the medication is taken out of the drawer, when it is being prepared, and at the bedside before administration to the patient. These checks occur before the medication is given and are part of the medication-safety process. Barcode technology can add an additional safety layer but does not replace the underlying medication-administration checks. B and C are incorrect because they place one or more label checks after administration rather than before the medication is given. D is incorrect because barcode scanning does not eliminate the third source-specified label comparison.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Identify the three medication-label check points used during preparation and administration: when the medication is removed from storage, during preparation, and at the bedside before administration.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests the three medication-label checks with one clearly correct timing sequence, balanced alternatives, current source verification, and no absolute-word or length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reproduces the three source-specified label-to-MAR checkpoints in the correct sequence before administration.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. It shifts one comparison to after administration and documentation rather than completing all three checks before the medication is given.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Two post-administration checks cannot substitute for the source-specified preparation-phase checks.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Barcode scanning does not replace the third label-to-MAR comparison specified in the checklist.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely places all three comparisons at the source-specified pre-administration points; B-D omit or misplace at least one check.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel medication-check timing sequences of comparable length and specificity; the prior 'only' distractors and uniquely-long correct response were removed.
